findings.claim_or_location: Section 1, HLA-B*58:01/Allopurinol (line 19): 'odds ratios of ~74 in Asians and ~101 in non-Asians, with individual studies reporting ORs from ~44 to over 100; a meta-analytic estimate placed the association near OR 117.6 (95% CI 70.3-196.8). Pooled test performance across ~7,500 patients indicates ~78% sensitivity, ~96% specificity, and ~99% negative predictive value.'
findings.issue: Two full sentences of load-bearing quantitative claims (population-stratified odds ratios, a meta-analytic point estimate with 95% CI, and pooled sensitivity/specificity/NPV across a stated N of ~7,500 patients) carry NO inline [N, tag] anchor. The [3, mechanism_review] citation is attached to the preceding CPIC-recommendation sentence only; these specific numbers float without attribution. Every other variant subsection anchors its numerical claims to a citation (e.g., abacavir 0%/2.7% [1, rct]; carbamazepine sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV [2, mechanism_review]; FTO 0.36 kg/m^2 [7, cohort]). This is the one location where quantitative claims are untraceable.
findings.recommended_fix: Append an inline citation to each quantitative sentence. If the OR/meta-analysis/test-performance figures come from the CPIC 2015 allopurinol guideline, tag them [3, mechanism_review]; if the meta-analytic OR 117.6 (CI 70.3-196.8) originates from a distinct meta-analysis (e.g., a published HLA-B*58:01 SCAR meta-analysis), add that source as a new bibliography entry tagged [meta_analysis] and cite it inline. Do not leave numeric claims without an inline [N, tag].
